persona: Calm and matter-of-fact; starts the claim without signing in and signs in when it is time to upload. Has a photo of the cut lock, the Police confirmation and a receipt the bike shop emailed after the theft.
initial_message: Hi, my electric bike was stolen from my front deck on Tuesday evening, 1 September. It was locked to the deck railing with a cable lock and someone cut the lock. I have reported it to the Police. I would like to make a claim on my contents insurance.

facts.incident.description: I got home at about 6pm and locked my e-bike to the front deck railing with a cable lock, as I usually do. At about 9:30pm I went out to bring it inside and it was gone. The cable lock had been cut and was left hanging on the railing.
facts.theft.entry_context: Nobody got into the house. The bike was on the front deck and the cable lock was cut.
facts.loss.description: Electric bike stolen from the front deck

contents.items.contents.item.description: Electric commuter bike, medium frame, grey

facts.contents.receipt_availability: A receipt from the bike shop, available now
facts.policyholder.name: Aria Kowhaiford
facts.evidence.photos: One photo of the cut cable lock on the deck railing. Available now.
facts.evidence.police: The Police report confirmation. Available now.
facts.evidence.receipt: The receipt the bike shop emailed me. Available now.
facts.if_asked_about_receipt_date: I bought the bike in October last year. After it was stolen I asked the shop for a copy of the receipt, and this is what they emailed me.
facts.if_asked_about_the_lock: A steel cable lock through the frame and around a railing post. The cut lock is still here.
facts.if_asked_about_other_items: Nothing else was taken. The house was locked and nobody got inside.

materials.prompt: Realistic smartphone photo taken in the evening under an outdoor deck light: a thick black vinyl-coated steel cable lock hangs from the top rail of a grey-stained timber deck railing, cut clean through about a third of the way along its length, the frayed silver steel strands showing at both cut ends. The small plain black lock body dangles from one end of the cable. Damp timber deck boards below and a pot plant at the edge of the frame. Close-up, the cut cable in the centre of the frame. No people, no text, no logos.
materials.purpose: Shows the cut lock left behind by the theft

design.notes: The claimant gives an innocent explanation (the shop emailed a copy after the theft), but the receipt prints only one date and it is a purchase date after the loss, so the indicator fires. The explanation goes to staff with it (rules, section 3).

triage.rationale: The e-bike receipt (serial VC2-TST-3013) prints a date of purchase of 4 September 2026, three days after the theft on 1 September 2026, while the claimant says the bike was bought in October 2025. That is a strong indicator, so a person must look, and the receipt contradicts the statement whether or not the Agent asks about it. The amount (NZD 3,899) is under the threshold and every required material is supplied. Allowed but not required: the Agent may record that the bike may not be fully covered because the wording names bicycles as a category that may carry a sublimit and the schedule states none (coverage_unclear); the pack policy carries no lookup uncertainty marker. It does not change the class. The pack policy must be in the lookup (setup.policies_in_system).

ownership_doc_after_loss.basis: Receipt date of purchase 4 September 2026 is after the last possible incident day, 1 September 2026

quote_before_loss.basis: No quote or assessment in the pack

prior_claims_12m.basis: Starts anonymous and signs in before the first upload; the account has no earlier claims

policy_inception_30d.basis: The lookup holds only the current period start (1 April 2026), which changes at every renewal, so the system cannot see how new the policy is; today it is not checked. The original inception date in the pack design, 2021-04-01, is more than 30 days before the incident, so the rule would give clear.
